$comment: Opening-filler ('hat') and closing-elevation ('boot') sentence rules. position: head=first sentence only, tail=last sentence only, any=anywhere. Regexes are Python re syntax, applied with re.IGNORECASE. severity: 3=whole sentence is deletable filler, 2=needs rewriting with concrete anchors, 1=advisory.

patterns.message: Era-framing opener: reviewers do not need to be told what era this is. Start from the paragraph's actual claim.
"With the rise of ..." opener carries no information. Delete it, or replace with the specific dates and numbers behind that rise.
"In recent years": name the years, the publication count, or the adoption figure that makes the trend real.
"has attracted increasing attention": whose attention, measured how? Add citation counts or venue data, or cut the sentence.

patterns.regex: ^[^.!?]{0,50}plays? (?:an?|a critical|a crucial|a vital|a pivotal|an important|a key|a significant|an integral) [^.!?]{0,20}role[^.!?]{0,50}[.!?]
patterns.message: Opening "plays a crucial role" is an assertion of importance, not evidence of it. State what breaks without it.

patterns.regex: ^(?:It is (?:well[- ]known|widely (?:known|accepted|recognized)|common knowledge)|As is well known|Needless to say|It goes without saying)[^.!?]{0,70}[.!?]
patterns.message: "It is well known that": if it truly is, omit it; if it is not, cite a source.

patterns.regex: ^[A-Z][^.!?]{0,40}(?:is|refers to|is defined as|can be defined as|is a (?:type|class|form|kind) of)[^.!?]{0,30}(?:technique|approach|method|framework|paradigm|architecture|mechanism|process|phenomenon)[^.!?]{0,40}[.!?]
patterns.message: Textbook definition opener: drop it if the reader already has this background, or fold it into the surrounding text.
Generic "existing methods still suffer from limitations": name the paper, the metric, and the size of the gap.
Closing significance claim: the paragraph loses nothing if you delete this sentence.
"holds great promise" ending: keep it only if this paragraph supplied the numbers that justify the promise.
"paves the way for future work" is self-congratulation reviewers read as padding. Cut it.
"provides valuable insights": any paper can claim this, so it says nothing. Replace with the specific finding.
"demonstrates the effectiveness of": give the metric and the delta instead of the verdict.
"requires further investigation": if this is a real limitation of your work, state which one; otherwise delete.

patterns.regex: ^(?:In (?:conclusion|summary|short|brief|essence)|To (?:conclude|summarize|sum up)|Overall|All in all|All things considered|Taken together|On the whole|Ultimately)[^a-z]
patterns.message: Explicit summary connector: a clear paragraph does not need to announce that it is now summarizing.

patterns.regex: ^(?:Looking (?:ahead|forward)|(?:As we )?[Mm]oving forward|Going forward|In the future|In the years to come)[^.!?]{0,80}[.!?]\s*$
patterns.message: Forward-looking closer belongs in the conclusion, and only with a concrete plan.

patterns.regex: \b(?:[Ii]t is worth (?:noting|mentioning|emphasizing|highlighting|pointing out)|[Ii]t (?:is|should be) (?:important|essential|crucial|necessary) to (?:note|mention|emphasize|highlight|point out)|[Ii]t should be (?:noted|emphasized|mentioned|pointed out))\b[^.!?]{0,10}that\b
patterns.message: "It is worth noting that": delete the clause and the sentence still reads correctly. It only announces attention.

patterns.regex: \b(?:delv(?:e|es|ing) into|navigat(?:e|es|ing) the (?:complexit(?:y|ies)|intricacies|landscape)|harness(?:es|ing)? the power of|unlock(?:s|ing)? the (?:potential|power)|embark(?:s|ing)? on (?:a|this) journey|at the forefront of|the intersection of|a testament to|the ever[- ](?:changing|evolving)|in the realm of)\b
patterns.message: Signature LLM vocabulary (delve into, harness the power of, navigate the complexities): replace with a plain verb.
Inflated adjective typical of generated prose: state the magnitude instead of the superlative.
"not only ... but also": a highly symmetric construction LLMs overuse. Split into two sentences of unequal length.
"By leveraging X, we achieve Y": a symmetric prepositional frame. Use an active verb and the concrete result.
Degree adverb + improvement verb with no number: state by how much, on which benchmark.

patterns.regex: \b(?:[Rr]esearch(?:ers)? (?:has|have) shown|[Ss]tudies have (?:shown|demonstrated|found)|[Pp]rior work has shown|[Ee]vidence suggests|[Ii]t has been shown)\b(?![^.!?]{0,40}\{\{CITE)
patterns.message: "Studies have shown" with no citation: add the reference or drop the claim.
"Many researchers argue": cite the specific works rather than hiding behind a collective noun.
"real-world scenarios": name the setting and the specific perturbations involved.
"strong robustness": report the perturbation range and how far the metric moved.
"achieves state-of-the-art performance" with no figure: give the metric, the number, and the baseline it beats.

patterns.regex: \b(?:[Ii]n other words|[Tt]hat is to say|[Pp]ut (?:differently|another way)|[Ss]imply put|[Tt]o put it (?:simply|differently))\b[,]?
patterns.message: "In other words": if the previous sentence was clear this is redundant; if it was not, rewrite that sentence.
"This underscores the importance of": a filler inference step. State the consequence directly.
"increasingly important": quantify the trend or give the interval over which it holds.
"cannot be overstated": show the consequence of ignoring it rather than asserting its weight.
Three-plus parallel abstract nouns: a hallmark LLM rhythm. Break the list or convert it to bullets.
Copula dodge ("serves as a crucial"): use the plain verb and say what it does.
Rhetorical question: academic prose rarely needs self-posed questions. Give the claim.
Stacked hedges ("may potentially"): keep one hedge, not two.
